attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence summarising the linked CNN report. He states it as fact in his own voice, so it counts as his claim.

semantics.note: The proposition matches the statement: a deepfaked cast that included the CFO scammed a company out of about $25M. 'On a video call' comes from the quote and link in the same post.

contract.note: Reading $25M as an approximate US-dollar figure (reported as US$25.6M) is ordinary and fair. Not requiring live interaction is also fair, because the statement does not claim real-time generation.

evidence.note: CNN, May 2024: police describe a fake CFO and fake colleagues on the video call; HK$200M, about $25.6M, was sent; Arup confirms fake voices and images were used.
SCMP, Feb 2024, citing police: everyone on the call except the victim was fake, including a recreated CFO; HK$200M (US$25.6M) was lost.

Government account confirms a deepfaked, prerecorded conference impersonating the CFO and a loss of about HK$200M, with later instructions sent by messaging. It gives HKD only and does not undercut the claim.

reviews.rationale: Police-sourced reports agree that a fabricated video conference with a fake CFO and fake colleagues led to transfers of HK$200M, about US$25.6M. That fits 'about $25 million'. The prerecorded format and follow-up messaging do not contradict the claim under the contract.

attribution.note: Marcus's own description of the employee in the incident he linked.

semantics.note: The proposition captures the claim that the scam worked on an employee who was initially suspicious.

contract.note: Reading 'not naive' as emphasis on his initial suspicion, not a verdict on his character, is a fair and ordinary reading.

evidence.note: CNN, Feb 2024, citing Supt Baron Chan: the worker first suspected a phishing email, dropped his doubts after the video call, and agreed to remit HK$200M.

reviews.rationale: The police account reported by CNN gives the sequence the contract requires: initial suspicion of phishing, reassurance from the apparent colleagues on the call, then the transfers. No evidence in the packet contradicts this.
